toml:
# DVB-S2 adaptive coding and modulation (ACM) along one satellite's passes over one station.
# Along a pass the slant range and elevation change, so the downlink Es/N0 changes. The run
# picks, at each step, the most efficient MODCOD whose ETSI EN 302 307-1 Table 13 threshold
# plus an implementation margin the link clears. It reports each pass's Es/N0 range and the
# data volume ACM moves, against the constant-coding baseline that closes at the mask
# elevation and the longest range.
#
# Every number below is ILLUSTRATIVE: no operator's orbit, station or link budget. MODELLED.
kind = "acm-link"
epoch = [2024.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
duration_hours = 12.0
step_s = 30.0
refraction = true
light_time = true

[link]
frequency_ghz = 8.2            # X-band downlink
eirp_dbw = 7.0
symbol_rate_msps = 20.0
other_losses_db = 2.0
zenith_atm_loss_db = 0.3
implementation_margin_db = 1.0
acm_step_s = 10.0

[satellite]
name = "eo-sso-a"
altitude_km = 550.0
inclination_deg = 97.6
raan_deg = 0.0
arg_lat_deg = 0.0
backlog_mbit = 400000.0
priority = 2.0

[station]
name = "mid-latitude"
lat_deg = 52.2
lon_deg = 5.0
alt_m = 10.0
mask_deg = 5.0
g_over_t_db = 30.0
setup_s = 120.0
summary: acm-link: 3 pass(es); ACM 92866 Mbit vs CCM 8PSK 3/4 58495 Mbit -> gain x1.59 (MODELLED)
